title: The waterfall and FT8
idea: A waterfall shows frequency across, time running down and strength as brightness. FT8 is 8-tone FSK in 15-second slots: keep your clock right and answer in the other slot.

rows: SNR of +3 dB in a 2.5 kHz bandwidth
Decodes at very low signal-to-noise ratios
Frequency across, time down, strength = intensity

compare.how: You both transmit at once; neither hears the other.
You send while they listen. Pick a clear frequency.
Signal-to-noise in 2.5 kHz, not an S-meter reading.

traps.wrong: Find a clear frequency during the same time slot as the calling station
traps.why: In the same slot they're transmitting too, so they can't hear you.

traps.wrong: Always call on the station’s frequency
traps.why: Calling on their own frequency piles everyone on one spot; find a clear one.
A sound card interface is enough; the must-have is a clock right to about 1 second.

traps.wrong: The signal is 3 dB over S9
traps.why: FT8 reports are signal-to-noise in 2.5 kHz, not S units.

traps.wrong: Frequency is horizontal, signal strength is vertical, time is intensity
traps.why: That's a spectrum display. On a waterfall time runs down and strength is the brightness.
Too much modulation, not too little, splatters lines either side.
